chunks: What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

About a man whose eyes overcame him with sleep, or some matter hindered him, from performing the obligatory prayer of dawn between the time dawn rises and the sun rises—and that is specifically regarding the obligatory prayer. If he has prayed one rak'ah of the morning prayer and then the sun rises, then let him complete it, and his prayer is valid.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, marking the end of fajr prayer time here
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer, meaning salat al-fajr
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn; the beginning time of the fajr prayer
key_terms.جَازَتْ: was valid and legally sufficient in fulfillment

ai.seo_question: If sunrise begins after one rak'ah of fajr, does the prayer still count?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the time of the obligatory salat of fajr. It indicates that if a person begins the prayer before sunrise and completes one rak'ah, then the prayer is to be completed and is counted as valid.
